title: Cohort-based Output Drift Detector for Config/Model Changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We occasionally see structured-output regressions (missing fields, type drift, enum skew) after model or config changes. Existing evals run bulk dataset diffs and per-field metrics, but they are noisy for low-frequency field combinations and do not tie directly to deployment events. Goal: implement a cohort-based detector that automatically snapshots field-level behavior anchored to config or model-change events, and raises prioritized alerts if statistically significant regressions are detected in cohorts that matter to customers. The detector should operate at canary and full-rollout levels, respect sampling budgets, and surface example-level failures with source request links for fast debugging. Design considerations include choice of statistical test, smoothing/priors for low-count cohorts, overlap handling between cohorts, backfill behavior for retroactive comparisons, and integration with Console alerting and rollouts. This ticket covers the backend detector, ingestion hooks from deployment events, and the wiring to evaluation artifacts and alert channels.
acceptance_criteria: Detector ingests model/config-change events and anchors baseline window automatically
Detector computes per-cohort per-field metrics (presence rate, type match rate, enum distribution) and stores time-series
Anomaly rule engine flags regressions using configurable thresholds and effect-size-aware tests (e.g., A/B test or Bayesian posterior delta)
Canary mode runs at deploy time: if a flagged regression exceeds severity threshold, the deployment receives an automatic rollback suggestion and a canary-blocking alert in Console
Detector surfaces up to 20 representative failing examples (with pointer to original request ID, prompt, and model variant) for each flagged cohort
Dashboard exists with cohort explorer, delta heatmap, and per-field ROC-style history for the last 30 days
Unit and integration tests cover edge cases: zero-count cohorts, backfilled data, multi-field correlated regressions
steps: Define cohort key semantics (prefixes, field combinations, traffic slice labels)
Extend eval ingestion pipeline to tag incoming samples with deployment_event_id and cohort keys
Implement aggregation job to compute baseline and candidate windows per cohort and field
Prototype statistical tests and select fallback for low-count cohorts (Bayesian smoothing + minimum effect size)
Add alert rule configuration and severity mapping in the alerts service
Expose results through a Console endpoint and build a basic cohort explorer widget (POC)
Wire canary gating hook: reject/flag rollout when canary regressions exceed policy
Create dashboards and an alert runbook pointing to example record links and rollback steps
recent_comments: 2026-03-02 - Liam Chen: POC aggregation job ran on sample dataset. Early results show high variance for <100 requests cohorts. Decided to add Bayesian smoothing and a min-sample threshold. Next: implement posterior delta check.

2026-03-04 - Mei Gonzalez (PM): Prioritize canary blocking for critical fields used in billing and legal outputs. Added 'canary-critical' label to cohort definitions. We should make severity mapping editable per-customer in a later iteration.

2026-03-06 - Rajiv Kapoor (Data Scientist): Reviewed tests. Suggested using Dirichlet prior for enum distributions and reporting KL divergence + absolute delta to avoid false positives on rare categories.
2026-03-09 - Design (Ana Ruiz): Quick Console wireframe done for cohort explorer. Suggest showing example-level diffs inline (expected vs actual fields) and a copy-to-clipboard for repro prompts.

2026-03-10 - Security (Priya Iyer): Confirmed no new secrets stored. PII removal step required before example payloads are surfaced in public dashboards. Marking as follow-up to add scrubber to ingestion path.
